name: Tofersen
drug_class: Antisense oligonucleotide (RNase H-mediated SOD1 mRNA knockdown)
route_note: Intrathecal bolus by lumbar puncture: three loading doses two weeks apart, then every 28 days.

discovery.note: A 2'-MOE gapmer antisense oligonucleotide designed to degrade SOD1 mRNA in people with SOD1-mutation ALS.

tagline: First genetically targeted therapy for SOD1 familial ALS
summary: Tofersen is an intrathecal antisense oligonucleotide that lowers production of superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1) protein in people with ALS caused by SOD1 mutations. It was approved on the basis of reduced neurofilament light chain, a biomarker of neurodegeneration.
mechanism: Mutations in SOD1 cause roughly 2% of ALS through a toxic gain of function of the misfolded protein. Tofersen binds SOD1 messenger RNA and recruits RNase H1 to cleave it, reducing synthesis of both mutant and normal SOD1 protein in the central nervous system.
Lower SOD1 levels are accompanied by falling cerebrospinal fluid SOD1 and plasma neurofilament light chain concentrations, indicating reduced axonal injury.
uses: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in adults with a SOD1 gene mutation

history.title: SOD1 gene
history.detail: Rosen et al. (Nature) identify SOD1 mutations as a cause of familial ALS.

history.title: Phase 1/2 results
history.detail: Miller et al. (NEJM) report dose-dependent lowering of CSF SOD1.

history.title: VALOR
history.detail: Phase 3 (NEJM) misses its primary clinical endpoint at 28 weeks but shows reductions in SOD1 and neurofilament light chain, with trends to benefit in open-label extension.

history.title: FDA accelerated approval
history.detail: In April the FDA grants accelerated approval based on neurofilament reduction.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: The European Commission authorises Qalsody under exceptional circumstances.

common: Raised CSF white cells and protein

facts: Tofersen was the first ALS drug approved by the FDA on the basis of a biomarker (plasma neurofilament light chain) reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.
